name: itsdangerous
note: holdout2: a second held-out set, written from the source at this commit after the dev and test sets had been used repeatedly. Every question is about a fact none of the twenty questions in eval/questions/itsdangerous.json asks about, and none is a rewording of one. expected_files are paths relative to the repo root; a retrieved record counts as relevant if its file is in the list. Scored once, after the configuration was chosen on dev.

questions.question: Is a signature compared in a way that does not leak timing information?
Can I check a signed value and get back true or false instead of catching an exception?
Why is the SHA-1 function looked up only when it is needed rather than when the module is imported?
What salt is used when the caller does not pass one?
How does the code work out whether the data serializer produces text or binary output?
How do I write a signed value straight into an open file and read it back out again?
Can a single call decode a payload with a different serializer than the one stored on the class?
What extra information does the error for a malformed header carry?
Why are the remaining signers not tried once a token turns out to be too old?
Which names can be imported straight from the top level of the package?
